title: 2D and 3D CNNs on total body photography compared with dermatologists for melanoma
summary: In a prospective study of 1690 melanocytic lesions in 143 high-risk patients, 2D and 3D CNN risk scores were compared with dermatologists against histopathology. The 3D-CNN had sensitivity 90.0%, specificity 64.6% and AUC 0.92, matching dermatologists' sensitivity of 90% but with lower specificity (dermatologists 92.3%); the 2D-CNN performed worse (sensitivity 70%, specificity 40%). Automated naevus counts differed from the gold standard (210 lesions versus 469 for 3D and 1324 for 2D), and excision decisions were partly guided by the CNN.
ai_technology: 2D (FotoFinder) and 3D (Vectra WB360) convolutional neural network classifiers on total body photography

evidence.tested: Prospective real-world comparison of CNN risk scores with dermatologists and histopathology in 143 patients.
evidence.unknown: Performance on larger numbers of melanomas, given excision partly guided by the CNN; commercial systems; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: CNNs scored melanocytic lesions and counted naevi on total body photographs.
